canonical_title: Airspeed response due to pitch attitude changes

versions.title_at_revision: Airspeed response due to pitch attitude changes
versions.text:
Standard: The air vehicle's airspeed does not diverge when the pitch attitude is disturbed from trim, unless the time for the airspeed perturbation to double amplitude following a disturbance from trim is greater than six seconds, and further modified as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Relaxation in Transonic Flight paragraph. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis and simulation to assess the air vehicle's airspeed response due to pitch attitude changes as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Direction of Speed Change paragraph and Relaxation in Transonic Flight paragraph, for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess the air vehicle's airspeed response due to pitch attitude changes as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Direction of Speed Change paragraph and Relaxation in Transonic Flight paragraph, for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess the air vehicle's airspeed response due to pitch attitude changes as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Direction of Speed Change paragraph and Relaxation in Transonic Flight paragraph, for selected combinations of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions.
